name: Central Saanich

seo.title: Central Saanich Landscaping & Grounds Care | RNC
seo.description: Grounds care for Keating business parks, village homes and farms, plus planting, irrigation and Erosion District-aware tree work. Get a free quote.

cardSummary: Brentwood Bay, Saanichton, farmland and the Keating business area, with an Erosion District that changes the tree rules.
intro: Central Saanich mixes farmland and village life: Brentwood Bay on Saanich Inlet, Saanichton’s main street, open fields across the peninsula, and the Keating business and industrial area.

The District protects dogwood, arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific yew, shore pine and trembling aspen, and any tree over 0.6 m in diameter. In the Erosion District, removing any tree needs an engineering permit and a geotechnical report. See [grounds maintenance](/services/grounds-maintenance/) or [get a free quote](/free-quote/?area=central-saanich).
propertyTypes: industrial and commercial sites in Keating
localRulesIntro: Central Saanich has a designated Erosion District, where any tree removal needs an engineering permit and a geotechnical report. Elsewhere, protected species need an application with a site plan.

localNotes.title: Central Saanich tree protection
localNotes.text: Central Saanich protects dogwood, arbutus, Garry oak, Pacific yew, shore pine and trembling aspen, nesting trees, permit-retained trees and any tree over 0.6 m diameter. Pruning or removing a protected tree needs an application with a site plan (an arborist report may be required); removing any tree in the Erosion District needs an Engineering permit and geotechnical report.

localNotes.title: CRD lawn-watering schedule
localNotes.text: CRD Stage 1 watering rules run May 1 to September 30 for properties on the regional water supply: lawns may be watered on Wednesdays and Saturdays (even addresses) or Thursdays and Sundays (odd addresses), 4-10 am or 7-10 pm; hand watering and drip irrigation of trees, shrubs and gardens is allowed any day. Multi-unit complexes use the complex's street address. New sod or seed does not need a permit and has a temporary schedule.

localNotes.title: Invasive plants and disposal
localNotes.text: The CRD Regional Invasive Species Program lists priority species (including giant hogweed, knotweed, gorse, poison hemlock, shiny geranium and yellow toadflax) and asks for sightings to be reported. Invasive plants must be disposed of properly: Hartland Landfill takes them bagged and labelled or in covered loads, and knotweed needs a controlled waste permit and is not accepted at municipal yard-waste drop-offs.

conditions.title: Open fields and wind
conditions.body: Farmland and rural lots on the open peninsula take steady wind. Hedgerows and windbreaks protect gardens, and they need regular trimming to stay dense.

conditions.title: Inlet slopes in Brentwood Bay
conditions.body: Lots that fall toward Saanich Inlet can be steep. If a property may be in the Erosion District, clearing on the slope should wait until that is confirmed.

conditions.title: Deer and farm edges
conditions.body: Deer move between fields and gardens, so new planting near rural edges is chosen or fenced with that in mind.

conditions.title: Business-park frontages
conditions.body: Keating sites need tidy frontages, parking islands and boulevard edges on a set schedule that works around deliveries and staff hours.

topServices.why: Keating business parks and rural homes both want scheduled frontage, hedge and mowing work.
Protected native species and the Erosion District mean tree work here starts with knowing which rules apply to the lot.

servicesBlurb.grounds-maintenance: Grounds care for business parks in Keating, village homes and stratas.
servicesBlurb.landscape-installation: Planting and hardscape for village lots and rural homes.
servicesBlurb.irrigation: Irrigation repairs and seasonal service for homes and commercial sites.
servicesBlurb.tree-vegetation: Tree work with protected species and the Erosion District checked first.

jobNotes.title: Slope planting kept, ivy pulled
jobNotes.body: On a lot near the Erosion District boundary, native slope planting was left in place and English ivy was pulled by hand instead of clearing the bank.

jobNotes.title: Hobby-farm frontage on a monthly round
jobNotes.body: A roadside hedgerow was trimmed and the verge mown monthly through the growing season, with the windbreak left full on the field side.

cta.heading: Get a free quote in Central Saanich
cta.body: Tell us whether it is a home, farm or business site, and if the lot slopes toward the inlet. That helps us check the Erosion District question early.
